headline: Watertight mesh: what it is and how to make a 3D model watertight
metaTitle: Watertight Mesh: What It Means & How to Fix It (2026 Slicer Guide)
metaDescription: A watertight mesh is a completely sealed 3D surface with no holes or gaps. Learn why Bambu & Cura demand it, how to verify it, and 4 ways to make an STL watertight.
shortDefinition: A watertight mesh (also known as a closed 2-manifold surface) is a 3D digital model whose outer polygonal surface completely encloses a continuous, solid volume without any holes, open seams, self-intersecting faces, or inverted normals. If you poured water inside the model, none would leak out. Slicers require a watertight mesh to distinguish solid interior infill from empty outside space.

quickAnswers.question: What makes a mesh watertight?
quickAnswers.answer: Every edge must connect exactly two triangles (2-manifold), all face normals must point outward, and the boundary must form a continuous sealed surface without open seams.

quickAnswers.question: Can you 3D print a non-watertight mesh?
quickAnswers.answer: Rarely. Slicers will guess what is inside versus outside, resulting in missing wall perimeters, infill leaking out into thin air, or slicer slice calculation failures.

quickAnswers.question: Fastest way to fix a non-watertight mesh?
quickAnswers.answer: Run an automated cloud boundary-stitching repair, or in Blender select non-manifold traits (Shift+Ctrl+Alt+M) and execute Merge by Distance followed by Fill Holes.

content:
## The 3 Golden Rules of a Watertight Mesh

A 3D model isn't watertight just because it looks solid in your viewport shading. Slicers evaluate geometry using mathematical topology rather than visual appearance. A mathematically watertight mesh strictly satisfies three criteria:

1. **Exact 2-Manifold Topology:** Every single edge must be shared by exactly two faces. If an edge touches only one face, it is an open hole (*boundary edge*). If it touches three or more, it contains an illegal interior wall (*T-junction*).
2. **Consistent Outward Normals:** Every polygonal face has a perpendicular vector (normal) defining which side is the exterior. Inverted or flipped normals cause the slicing engine to treat exterior walls as empty void.
3. **Zero Self-Intersections:** Surface shells cannot intersect or pierce through one another without welded intersecting vertex seams.

## Why slicers fail on non-watertight files

When you import an STL or 3MF file into Bambu Studio, Cura, or PrusaSlicer, the engine slices the 3D volume into hundreds of microscopic horizontal 2D planes. On each plane, it runs an **Odd-Even Winding Number** algorithm:

* The engine casts a ray from infinity toward the center of the print bed.
* Every time the ray crosses a boundary perimeter, the status toggles: *Outside → Inside → Outside → Inside*.
* If an edge is missing or unsealed, the ray enters the interior and never exits. The algorithm fails to close the polygon loop, leading to missing layer walls, infill leaking into the void, or the slicer throwing an `Error: Model is not watertight / manifold`.

## Common reasons meshes fail watertight tests

1. **Zero-Thickness Planes:** Modeling a cape, leaf, or logo curve as a 2D flat plane without an extruded solid wall thickness.
2. **Accidental Duplicate Vertices:** In Blender or Maya, pressing `E` (extrude) and right-clicking cancels movement but leaves un-welded duplicate vertices resting in the exact same coordinates.
3. **Boolean Union Artifacts:** Combining two overlapping CAD solids where coincident coplanar faces intersect without generating a continuous manifold joint.
4. **AI Text-to-3D Meshes:** Neural generators (Meshy, Tripo, CSM) frequently export multiple loose, overlapping triangle shells nested inside each other rather than a single unified outer hull.
5. **Photogrammetry & 3D Scans:** Areas occluded from scanner cameras (such as the base of a figurine) remain open boundary loops.

## How to fix non-watertight meshes (4 Methods)

### Method 1 — Automated Cloud Diagnosis & Repair (2 Minutes)
Upload your STL, GLB or zipped OBJ to TEELI's diagnostic check. It inspects open boundary loops, non-manifold edges, flipped normals, and scale verification in real time, repairing topology without stripping color layers or UV coordinates.

:::callout
**Free Diagnostic Check on TEELI:** Upload STL, OBJ, GLB or a ZIP to verify open holes, inverted normals, duplicate vertices, and scale before slicing.
[Launch Free Check →](https://app.teeli.net/?utm_source=teeli.net&utm_medium=glossary&utm_campaign=watertight)
:::

### Method 2 — Manual Repair in Blender (Full Control)
1. Select your object, press `Tab` for Edit Mode, then press `Alt+A` to deselect all geometry.
2. Go to **Select → Select All by Trait → Non Manifold** (`Shift+Ctrl+Alt+M`). All unsealed edges and open holes highlight in orange.
3. Press `M` → **By Distance** to weld duplicated vertices together.
4. Press `Alt+F` to fill open boundary loops, or use **Mesh → Clean Up → Fill Holes**.
5. Press `Shift+N` to recalculate normals outward.
6. Verify with the **3D-Print Toolbox** extension (`N-panel → 3D-Print → Check All → Non Manifold Edge: 0`).

### Method 3 — In-Slicer Automatic Repair (Windows Only)
In Bambu Studio or Orca Slicer, right-click the warning notification and select **Fix model**. In PrusaSlicer, click the warning triangle to trigger Windows Netfabb repair. *Caution: Auto-repair services rebuild triangle sets and will often strip painted multi-color data from 3MF files.*

### Method 4 — Voxel Remeshing (Last Resort)
When a model suffers from thousands of micro-fractures, applying a Voxel Remesher (Blender Remesh modifier or Meshmixer *Make Solid*) generates a fresh shrink-wrapped manifold outer shell. *Trade-off: Voxel remeshing softens sharp mechanical tolerances and destroys UV texture coordinates.*

faq.question: What is the difference between manifold and watertight?
faq.answer: In 3D printing terminology, manifold and watertight are practically synonymous. A 2-manifold closed surface is the mathematical definition of a watertight 3D solid.

faq.question: Can a hollow model be watertight?
faq.answer: Yes. A hollow object (like a mug or hollow figurine) is completely watertight as long as the outer and inner walls form a continuous, sealed surface with measurable wall thickness.

faq.question: Why does my STL look closed in CAD but shows as non-watertight in the slicer?
faq.answer: Tessellation tolerance. When CAD software exports smooth NURBS surfaces into flat triangular STL facets, tiny rounding tolerances can leave micro-gaps between adjacent curves.

faq.question: How do inverted normals break watertightness?
faq.answer: While vertices may be connected, a triangle with inverted normals informs the slicing engine that solid matter exists on the outside. Slicers invert infill or fail to generate perimeters.

faq.question: How do I check if my STL is watertight for free?
faq.answer: You can inspect it in Blender using the 3D-Print Toolbox Check All tool, or upload it to TEELI /check for an instant browser diagnostic report.
